title: AMD Is On Track to Beat Lisa Su’s $100 Billion Revenue Prediction By 2 Years
excerpt: Lisa Su set a bold target for AMD to hit $100 billion in annual revenue by 2030, but Wall Street analysts now see a very different timeline taking shape as A...
content_html:
Rich Duprey

Mon, July 27, 2026 at 10:50 AM CDT 5 min read

Quick Read

  • Wall Street forecasts AMD hitting Lisa Su's $100 billion revenue target by 2028, two years ahead of her original 2030 goal.

  • AMD's upcoming MI450 accelerator and Helios rack system aim to establish Instinct as the dominant second-source GPU for hyperscale AI clusters.

  • Analysts project a 66% average annual EPS growth rate over five years, tripling AMD's 2025 revenue without requiring it to overtake Nvidia.

  • Act now: the analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just named his top 10 AI stocks — and AMD didn't make the cut. Grab the names FREE today.

Artificial intelligence spending continues to reshape the semiconductor industry. Hyperscale cloud providers are committing hundreds of billions of dollars to AI infrastructure, and the market is beginning to look less like a winner-take-all race than many investors expected just two years ago. As inference workloads expand alongside AI training, customers increasingly want a second supplier capable of delivering cutting-edge accelerators at scale. That shift is creating an opportunity that simply didn't exist when Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) stood almost alone.

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) has moved from being an afterthought in AI GPUs to becoming a legitimate challenger. While it still trails Nvidia by a wide margin, Wall Street is beginning to price in a future where AMD captures enough of the exploding AI market to become a permanent fixture in hyperscale data centers. If those forecasts prove accurate, CEO Lisa Su's ambitious goal of reaching $100 billion in annual revenue by 2030 may arrive much sooner than expected.

AMD's Next Generation Could Be the Catalyst

AMD's AI story barely existed a few years ago. Today, its Instinct accelerators are winning deployments at many of the world's largest cloud providers, and the next generation of products could accelerate that momentum.

According to AMD's product roadmap, the forthcoming MI450 accelerator and Helios AI rack system are designed to compete for larger-scale AI deployments. Rather than selling individual chips, AMD is increasingly offering integrated rack-scale solutions that mirror how hyperscalers now build AI clusters.

That matters because inference demand is expanding rapidly. Training large language models remains important, but serving billions of AI queries every day requires enormous computing capacity. No single supplier is likely to satisfy all of that demand.

  • 华尔街预测 AMD 将在 2028 年实现 Lisa Su 的 1000 亿美元收入目标，比她最初的 2030 年目标提前了两年。
  • AMD 即将推出的 MI450 加速器和 Helios 机架系统旨在将 Instinct 打造成超大规模 AI 集群的主导第二来源 GPU。
  • 分析师预计，五年内每股收益年均增长率将达到 66%，AMD 到 2025 年的收入将增加两倍，而无需超越 Nvidia。
  • 立即行动：2010 年给 NVIDIA 打电话的分析师刚刚列出了他心目中的十大人工智能股票，而 AMD 却没有上榜。 今天免费获取名字。

人工智能支出持续重塑半导体行业。 超大规模云提供商正在向人工智能基础设施投入数千亿美元，而市场开始看起来不像许多投资者两年前预期的那样是一场赢家通吃的竞赛。 随着推理工作负载随着人工智能培训的扩展，客户越来越希望有第二家能够大规模提供尖端加速器的供应商。 这种转变正在创造一个机会，而当英伟达（纳斯达克股票代码：NVDA）几乎孤军奋战时，这个机会根本就不存在。

Advanced Micro Devices（纳斯达克股票代码：AMD）已经从人工智能 GPU 领域的后起之秀转变为真正的挑战者。 尽管AMD仍远远落后于Nvidia，但华尔街已经开始预计AMD将占领足够的爆炸性人工智能市场，成为超大规模数据中心的永久固定装置。 如果这些预测准确，首席执行官苏姿丰 (Lisa Su) 到 2030 年年收入达到 1000 亿美元的雄心勃勃的目标可能会比预期早得多实现。

AMD 的下一代可能成为催化剂

AMD 的人工智能故事在几年前还几乎不存在。 如今，其 Instinct 加速器正在赢得许多全球最大的云提供商的部署，而下一代产品可能会加速这一势头。

根据AMD的产品路线图，即将推出的MI450加速器和Helios AI机架系统旨在争夺更大规模的AI部署。 AMD 不再销售单独的芯片，而是越来越多地提供集成的机架规模解决方案，反映了超大规模企业现在构建人工智能集群的方式。

立即行动：2010 年给 NVIDIA 打电话的分析师刚刚列出了他心目中的十大人工智能股票，而 AMD 却没有上榜。 今天免费获取名字。

这很重要，因为推理需求正在迅速扩大。 训练大型语言模型仍然很重要，但每天处理数十亿个人工智能查询需要巨大的计算能力。 没有任何一家供应商能够满足所有这些需求。
